$comment: Shared contract for query -> stored-value matching. TWO implementations read this file:
- plugins/functions/mcp-server/src/lib/cohortValueResolver.ts   (Deno, deep-link surface)
- plugins/ui/apps/vue-mri-ui-lib/src/ai/valueResolution.ts      (browser, pa_* WebMCP tools)
They cannot share a module (different runtimes, nothing crosses that boundary in this repo), so
this table is what keeps them in step. A ranking change belongs HERE first, then in both files —
if you add it to only one suite, the other surface silently degrades and nothing fails.
THE RULES, best match first. Each is a property of the two strings or of the column, not a list
of terms someone thought of, so they hold on a dataset nobody here has seen:
0  the row IS the term            after casing and demographic-synonym expansion
1  the row CONTAINS the term      as a substring, 3+ characters
2  the term ABBREVIATES the row   read from the row's FIRST word, each query word consuming
either the next row word or the initials of the next several
…or the row IS the term's CODE the same initials rule read the other way ('F' <- Female)
3  every DISTINCTIVE word is present
4  some distinctive word is present
A word is distinctive when it separates one row of THIS column from another — measured as the
share of rows carrying it (>= 60%, over columns of 4+ rows, is filler). Below that the rules fall
back to a small seeded list, because a frequency over two rows means nothing.
Two things stay seeded and cannot be derived: demographic synonyms ('women' -> 'female'; no
structure gets you there) and abbreviations whose expansion is NOT in the row ('ICU' where the
column says 'Intensive Care'). The seeds also drive the blind-retry path, which has no rows to
measure — an abbreviation cannot be inverted into a search term without a lexicon.
`rows` use a neutral shape { value, label }; each side maps it onto its own row type. Row counts
matter: a case written with two rows is testing the seeded fallback, not the measured rule.
`expectedOrder` lists the `value` of every row that must match, best first. An empty list means
nothing may match. `alternateQueries` cases assert the retry queries used when the attribute's
domain cannot be enumerated.

ranking.name: an exact token beats a longer value that merely contains it
casing alone never hides a value
ranking.why: The /values search runs a case-sensitive LIKE in the database.

ranking.name: the value column is matched too, not only the label
a demographic synonym resolves to the stored token
ranking.why: The user says "women"; the column stores "F". Never ask the user how their data spells it. Not derivable — this one is seeded.

ranking.name: a term reaches a row it is not a substring of, by abbreviating it
ranking.why: The reported failure: the /values search found nothing and the assistant reported the value absent.

ranking.name: an acronym no list contains still reaches its expansion
ranking.why: The point of deriving the rule: NICU is in no table here, and neither will be whatever a given dataset uses (ASC, LTACH, PCP). The initials must come out of the row itself.

ranking.name: initials are read from the START of the row, never from inside it
ranking.why: Precision over recall, the same trade this module makes everywhere: reading initials from anywhere inside a row lets an acronym claim rows it does not name, and a near-miss value is a silent clinical error. A row an acronym does not reach is still shown — nothing matching returns the whole column.

ranking.name: a seeded abbreviation covers an expansion the row does not spell out
ranking.why: The column says "Intensive Care"; there is no "U" in the row to derive the U of ICU from. This is why the seed list still exists.

ranking.name: a coded column is reached by the term's own initials
ranking.why: Not a demographics rule: marital status, discharge status and yes/no flags are all stored as bare letters, and no synonym table can enumerate them. The row's code has to be derived FROM the term.

ranking.name: a word nearly every row carries stops discriminating
ranking.why: "Visit" cannot tell you which visit type is meant when four rows in five say it.

ranking.name: the same word still discriminates in a column that does not repeat it
ranking.why: The converse, and the reason filler is measured rather than listed: here "visit" is what separates one row from the other, so the row carrying it must rank first.

ranking.name: a column too short to measure falls back to the seeded filler words
ranking.why: Two rows is not a frequency. Without the fallback "visit" would count as distinctive and the target row, which lacks it, would drop below a row that has nothing else in common.

ranking.name: a row sharing only one distinctive word ranks below the phrase matches
an unrelated term matches nothing rather than something close
ranking.why: A near-miss clinical concept is a silent clinical error; better to return the whole column.

ranking.name: an empty query matches nothing (the caller asks for the whole domain instead)

alternateQueries.name: a phrase the endpoint cannot match is retried by its expansions
alternateQueries.why: Title case first: a stored concept name usually looks like "Emergency Room Visit".

alternateQueries.name: casings are swept for a case-sensitive LIKE
bounded, so a failed search cannot fan out into many endpoint calls
alternateQueries.query: acute upper respiratory infection of the intensive care unit
